parts.label: a
hints: At least 3 pianists means the quintet can contain 3, 4, or 5 pianists.
Form combinations for each case: 3P 2S, 4P 1S, 5P 0S, and sum them.

walkthrough.text:
Partition into disjoint cases based on the number of pianists:
$$\text{3 pianists}: {}^6 C_3 \times {}^5 C_2 = 20 \times 10 = 200, \quad \text{4 pianists}: {}^6 C_4 \times {}^5 C_1 = 15 \times 5 = 75$$

Calculate the case of 5 pianists and sum all cases:
$$\text{5 pianists}: {}^6 C_5 \times {}^5 C_0 = 6 \times 1 = 6 \implies \text{Total} = 200 + 75 + 6 = 281$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Translate the lower bound into exhaustive cases of pianists:
$$\text{Pianists} \in \{3, 4, 5\}$$$

Sum the products across all three scenarios:
$$200 + 75 + 6 = 281$$

ai_rubric.observable: Partition into cases by pianist count: 3P 2S (6C3 * 5C2), 4P 1S (6C4 * 5C1), 5P 0S (6C5 * 5C0).
Sum the cases 200 + 75 + 6 to obtain 281 quintets.

parts.label: a
hints: At most 1 junior means the team contains either 0 juniors or 1 junior.
Calculate ways for 0 juniors (all 4 seniors) and 1 junior (1 junior and 3 seniors), then add.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the two disjoint cases for junior count:
$$\text{0 juniors}: {}^5 C_0 \times {}^7 C_4 = 1 \times 35 = 35, \quad \text{1 junior}: {}^5 C_1 \times {}^7 C_3 = 5 \times 35 = 175$$

Sum the two cases:
$$\text{Total teams} = 35 + 175 = 210$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
List the two valid junior quotas:
$$\text{Junior count} \in \{0, 1\}$$$

Add the counts from both outcomes:
$$35 + 175 = 210$$

ai_rubric.observable: Set up disjoint cases for 0 juniors (5C0 * 7C4) and 1 junior (5C1 * 7C3).
Sum the cases 35 + 175 to obtain 210 teams.

parts.label: a
hints: Use the complement method: subtract selections with fewer than 2 red balls from the total.
Total selections is ${}^{13}C_5$. Bad selections have 0 red or 1 red.

walkthrough.text:
Find total selections and the count of unacceptable selections (0 or 1 red):
$$\text{Total} = {}^{13}C_5 = 1287, \quad \text{0 red}: {}^5 C_5 = 1, \quad \text{1 red}: {}^8 C_1 \times {}^5 C_4 = 40$$

Subtract the bad selections from the total:
$$\text{Required selections} = 1287 - (1 + 40) = 1287 - 41 = 1246$$

ai_rubric.observable: Subtract cases with fewer than 2 red balls from total selections: 13C5 - 5C5 - (8C1 * 5C4).
Evaluate the difference 1287 - 41 to obtain 1246 selections.

parts.label: a
hints: Use the complement method: subtract single-colour selections from all selections.
Total selections is ${}^{13}C_4$. Monocolour selections can only be all silver or all black.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the total selections and the single-colour selections:
$$\text{Total} = {}^{13}C_4 = 715, \quad \text{All silver}: {}^6 C_4 = 15, \quad \text{All black}: {}^4 C_4 = 1$$

Subtract the single-colour selections from the total:
$$\text{Required selections} = 715 - (15 + 1) = 715 - 16 = 699$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Subtract monochrome sets from the unrestricted total:
$$\text{Selections} = \binom{13}{4} - \binom{6}{4} - \binom{4}{4}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Subtract single-colour selections from total selections: 13C4 - 6C4 - 4C4.
Evaluate the difference 715 - 16 to obtain 699 selections.

parts.label: a
hints: Strictly more men than women in a committee of 5 means men must number 3, 4, or 5.
Calculate combinations for 3M 2W, 4M 1W, and 5M 0W, then sum.

walkthrough.text:
Partition into cases where men outnumber women:
$$\text{3M 2W}: {}^7 C_3 \times {}^6 C_2 = 35 \times 15 = 525, \quad \text{4M 1W}: {}^7 C_4 \times {}^6 C_1 = 35 \times 6 = 210$$

Calculate the 5M 0W case and sum all cases:
$$\text{5M 0W}: {}^7 C_5 \times {}^6 C_0 = 21 \times 1 = 21 \implies \text{Total} = 525 + 210 + 21 = 756$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify majority cases for men in a group of 5:
$$\text{Men count} \in \{3, 4, 5\}$$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sum cases with 3 men (7C3 * 6C2), 4 men (7C4 * 6C1), and 5 men (7C5 * 6C0).
Sum the cases 525 + 210 + 21 to obtain 756 committees.

parts.label: a
hints: At least 5 of the same colour means either at least 5 red or all 5 blue (with 1 red).
Evaluate cases: 5R 1B, 6R 0B, and 1R 5B.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate selections with at least 5 red marbles:
$$\text{5R 1B}: {}^9 C_5 \times {}^5 C_1 = 126 \times 5 = 630, \quad \text{6R 0B}: {}^9 C_6 \times {}^5 C_0 = 84 \times 1 = 84$$

Calculate selections with 5 blue marbles and sum all cases:
$$\text{1R 5B}: {}^9 C_1 \times {}^5 C_5 = 9 \times 1 = 9 \implies \text{Total} = 630 + 84 + 9 = 723$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Group into monochromatic quotas: 5+ red or 5 blue:
$$\text{Cases}: \quad (5\text{R}, 1\text{B}), \; (6\text{R}, 0\text{B}), \; (1\text{R}, 5\text{B})$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sum cases for at least 5 of one colour: 5R 1B (9C5 * 5C1), 6R 0B (9C6), 1R 5B (9C1 * 5C5).
Sum the counts 630 + 84 + 9 to obtain 723 selections.

parts.label: a
hints: Choose 1 swimmer from 6 in ${}^6 C_1$ ways.
The remaining 6 athletes must contain at least 5 cyclists: either 5C 1R or 6C 0R.

walkthrough.text:
Fix 1 swimmer and split remaining 6 places into cyclist cases:
$$\text{Swimmer}: {}^6 C_1 = 6, \quad \text{5C 1R}: {}^8 C_5 \times {}^5 C_1 = 280, \quad \text{6C 0R}: {}^8 C_6 \times {}^5 C_0 = 28$$

Multiply swimmer choices by the sum of cyclist cases:
$$\text{Total teams} = 6 \times (280 + 28) = 6 \times 308 = 1848$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Combine the single swimmer with the two cyclist cases:
$$\text{Teams} = \binom{6}{1} \times \left[\binom{8}{5}\binom{5}{1} + \binom{8}{6}\binom{5}{0}\right]$$

ai_rubric.observable: Fix 1 swimmer (6C1) and multiply by cases for cyclists and runners: 5C 1R (8C5 * 5C1) and 6C 0R (8C6 * 5C0).
Evaluate 6 * (280 + 28) to obtain 1848 teams.

parts.label: b
hints: With 1 swimmer, cyclists (C) and runners (R) must sum to 6.
Conditions C >= 4 and R <= 2 give valid triples (S, C, R): (1,4,2), (1,5,1), (1,6,0).

walkthrough.text:
List valid cases (S, C, R) and compute counts:
$$(1,4,2): 6 \times {}^8 C_4 \times {}^5 C_2 = 4200, \quad (1,5,1): 6 \times {}^8 C_5 \times {}^5 C_1 = 1680$$

Calculate the (1,6,0) case and sum:
$$(1,6,0): 6 \times {}^8 C_6 \times {}^5 C_0 = 168 \implies \text{Total} = 4200 + 1680 + 168 = 6048$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Establish the three cases matching the runner and cyclist bounds:
$$\text{Cases}: \quad (1,4,2), \; (1,5,1), \; (1,6,0)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sum valid cases (S, C, R): (1,4,2) with 6 * 8C4 * 5C2, (1,5,1) with 6 * 8C5 * 5C1, (1,6,0) with 6 * 8C6 * 5C0.
Sum the cases 4200 + 1680 + 168 to obtain 6048 teams.

parts.label: a
hints: With exactly 3 archers, choose 3 remaining members from 6 bowlers and 4 climbers.
Each must have at least one member: cases are 2 bowlers, 1 climber or 1 bowler, 2 climbers.

walkthrough.text:
Choose 3 archers and split the other 3 places between bowlers and climbers:
$$\text{Archers}: {}^5 C_3 = 10, \quad \text{2B 1C}: {}^6 C_2 \times {}^4 C_1 = 60, \quad \text{1B 2C}: {}^6 C_1 \times {}^4 C_2 = 36$$

Multiply archer choices by the sum of bowler/climber combinations:
$$\text{Total teams} = 10 \times (60 + 36) = 10 \times 96 = 960$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Multiply archer combinations by the valid partitions of the remaining 3 places:
$$\text{Teams} = \binom{5}{3} \times \left[\binom{6}{2}\binom{4}{1} + \binom{6}{1}\binom{4}{2}\right]$$

ai_rubric.observable: Fix 3 archers (5C3) and choose remaining 3 from bowlers and climbers: 2B 1C (6C2 * 4C1) + 1B 2C (6C1 * 4C2).
Evaluate 10 * (60 + 36) to obtain 960 teams.

parts.label: b
hints: We require A + B + C = 6, with A >= 1, B >= 1, C >= 1, and B > C.
Since C >= 1, the smallest value of B is 2.
Find all valid integer triples (A, B, C) and compute the combinations for each.

walkthrough.text:
List all integer triples $(A, B, C)$ summing to 6 with $A, B, C \ge 1$ and $B > C$:
$$(3,2,1), \quad (2,3,1), \quad (1,4,1), \quad (1,3,2)$$

Evaluate the combination product for each case:
$$(3,2,1): 600, \quad (2,3,1): 800, \quad (1,4,1): 300, \quad (1,3,2): 600$$

Sum the four cases:
$$\text{Total teams} = 600 + 800 + 300 + 600 = 2300$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify valid triples (A, B, C) satisfying A + B + C = 6, all >= 1, and B > C: (3,2,1), (2,3,1), (1,4,1), (1,3,2).
Compute products 5CA * 6CB * 4CC for each case: 600, 800, 300, 600.
Sum the cases to obtain 2300 teams.

parts.label: a
hints: No bass players means all 6 musicians come from the 9 violinists and 5 cellists.
With at least 4 violinists, the cases are 4V 2C, 5V 1C, and 6V 0C.
Sum the counts from each case.

walkthrough.text:
Partition selections into violinist cases with 0 bass players:
$$\text{4V 2C}: {}^9 C_4 \times {}^5 C_2 = 1260, \quad \text{5V 1C}: {}^9 C_5 \times {}^5 C_1 = 630, \quad \text{6V 0C}: {}^9 C_6 \times {}^5 C_0 = 84$$

Sum the three cases:
$$\text{Total ensembles} = 1260 + 630 + 84 = 1974$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sum cases with 0 bass players: 4V 2C (9C4 * 5C2), 5V 1C (9C5 * 5C1), 6V 0C (9C6 * 5C0).
Sum the cases 1260 + 630 + 84 to obtain 1974 ensembles.

parts.label: b
hints: The constraints are V >= 4, C >= 1, B <= 1, summing to 6.
List the valid triples (V, C, B): (4,1,1), (4,2,0), (5,1,0).
Calculate combinations for each triple and sum.

walkthrough.text:
List the valid triples $(V, C, B)$ satisfying the constraints:
$$(4,1,1), \quad (4,2,0), \quad (5,1,0)$$

Evaluate the products for each triple:
$$(4,1,1): {}^9 C_4 \times {}^5 C_1 \times {}^3 C_1 = 1890, \quad (4,2,0): {}^9 C_4 \times {}^5 C_2 = 1260, \quad (5,1,0): {}^9 C_5 \times {}^5 C_1 = 630$$

Sum the cases:
$$\text{Total ensembles} = 1890 + 1260 + 630 = 3780$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify the three configurations fulfilling all musician requirements:
$$\text{Triples}: \quad (4,1,1), \; (4,2,0), \; (5,1,0)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify valid triples (V, C, B) satisfying V >= 4, C >= 1, B <= 1, and V + C + B = 6: (4,1,1), (4,2,0), (5,1,0).
Evaluate products for each case: 9C4 * 5C1 * 3C1, 9C4 * 5C2, 9C5 * 5C1.
Sum the cases 1890 + 1260 + 630 to obtain 3780 ensembles.

parts.label: a
hints: Exclude all Ls, leaving E (up to 3) and the 4 single letters {M, N, T, A}.
We need 5 letters with at least two Es: cases are 2 Es or 3 Es.
Count ways to complete each case from the 4 single letters.

walkthrough.text:
Exclude L, leaving letter types E (up to 3) and 4 singles $\{\text{M, N, T, A}\}$:
$$\text{Eligible pool}: \quad \text{E} \times 3, \; \{\text{M, N, T, A}\}$$

Partition 5-letter selections by count of E:
$$2\text{Es}: {}^4 C_3 = 4, \quad 3\text{Es}: {}^4 C_2 = 6$$

Sum the cases:
$$\text{Total selections} = 4 + 6 = 10$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Isolate E and single letters:
$$\text{Pool}: \quad \{\text{E, E, E, M, N, T, A}\}$$

Count completions for 2 Es and 3 Es:
$$4 + 6$$

ai_rubric.observable: Exclude L, leaving letter types E (up to 3) and 4 singles {M, N, T, A}.
Partition selections of 5 letters by count of E: 2 Es with 4C3 singles, 3 Es with 4C2 singles.
Sum the cases 4 + 6 to obtain 10 selections.

parts.label: b
hints: Allowed counts of E are 1, 2, or 3. Allowed counts of L are 0 or 1.
There are 6 possible pairs of counts (E, L): (1,0), (2,0), (3,0), (1,1), (2,1), (3,1).
Fill remaining slots for each pair from the 4 singles {M, N, T, A} and sum.

walkthrough.text:
Sum all cases:
$$\text{Total selections} = 1 + 4 + 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 25$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Tabulate all combinations of E and L:
$$(E, L) \in \{1,2,3\} \times \{0,1\}$$$

Compute the selections of singles for each pair:
$$1 + 4 + 6 + 4 + 6 + 4$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify 6 valid pairs of counts (E, L) with E in {1,2,3} and L in {0,1}: (1,0), (2,0), (3,0), (1,1), (2,1), (3,1).
Calculate combinations of singles for each case: 4C4, 4C3, 4C2, 4C3, 4C2, 4C1.
Sum the counts 1 + 4 + 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 to obtain 25 selections.

parts.label: a
hints: In a board of 6, strictly more women than men means women count 4, 5, or 6.
Form cases: 4W 2M, 5W 1M, 6W 0M.
Multiply combinations within each case and sum.

walkthrough.text:
Identify majority cases for women in a group of 6:
$$\text{4W 2M}: {}^6 C_4 \times {}^8 C_2 = 15 \times 28 = 420, \quad \text{5W 1M}: {}^6 C_5 \times {}^8 C_1 = 6 \times 8 = 48$$

Calculate the 6W 0M case:
$$\text{6W 0M}: {}^6 C_6 \times {}^8 C_0 = 1 \times 1 = 1$$

Sum all cases:
$$\text{Total boards} = 420 + 48 + 1 = 469$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Enumerate cases where women exceed men:
$$\text{Women} \in \{4, 5, 6\}$$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify valid distributions of women and men with W > M: 4W 2M, 5W 1M, 6W 0M.
Evaluate products 6CW * 8CM for each case: 15 * 28, 6 * 8, 1 * 1.
Sum the cases 420 + 48 + 1 to obtain 469 boards.

parts.label: b
hints: At least 2 men and at least 2 women means the distribution of (M, W) can be (2,4), (3,3), or (4,2).
Calculate the combinations for each of the three distributions.
Sum the counts across the three distributions.

walkthrough.text:
List the valid distributions of men and women:
$$(2\text{M}, 4\text{W}), \quad (3\text{M}, 3\text{W}), \quad (4\text{M}, 2\text{W})$$

Calculate combinations for each distribution:
$$(2\text{M}, 4\text{W}): 420, \quad (3\text{M}, 3\text{W}): {}^8 C_3 \times {}^6 C_3 = 1120, \quad (4\text{M}, 2\text{W}): {}^8 C_4 \times {}^6 C_2 = 1050$$

Sum the three cases:
$$\text{Total boards} = 420 + 1120 + 1050 = 2590$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Set up the three balanced gender cases:
$$\text{Distributions}: \quad (2,4), \; (3,3), \; (4,2)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify valid distributions with at least 2 of each gender: 2M 4W, 3M 3W, 4M 2W.
Evaluate products 8CM * 6CW for each case: 8C2 * 6C4, 8C3 * 6C3, 8C4 * 6C2.
Sum the cases 420 + 1120 + 1050 to obtain 2590 boards.

parts.label: a
hints: With no restrictions, choose 5 personnel from all 12 available staff.
Use the standard combination formula ${}^{12}C_5$.

walkthrough.text:
State the unrestricted combination formula:
$$\text{Committees} = {}^{12}C_5 = \frac{12!}{5!(12 - 5)!} = \frac{12!}{5! \times 7!}$$

Evaluate the arithmetic quotient:
$${}^{12}C_5 = \frac{12 \times 11 \times 10 \times 9 \times 8}{5 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 792$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Form an unconstrained team of 5 from 12 candidates:
$$\text{Committees} = \binom{12}{5}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Formulate 12C5 for unrestricted selection of 5 from 12 medical personnel.
Evaluate 12C5 to obtain 792 committees.

parts.label: b
hints: Use the complement: subtract committees with no doctors or no nurses from the total.
Total is 792 from part (a).
Committees with no doctors consists of all 5 nurses (${}^5 C_5 = 1$).
Committees with no nurses consists of 5 doctors from 7 (${}^7 C_5 = 21$).

walkthrough.text:
Find the bad cases violating the requirement:
$$\text{All nurses (0 doctors)}: {}^5 C_5 = 1, \quad \text{All doctors (0 nurses)}: {}^7 C_5 = 21$$

Subtract the bad cases from the unrestricted total:
$$\text{Required committees} = 792 - (1 + 21) = 792 - 22$$

Evaluate the difference:
$$\text{Total committees} = 770$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Use the complement approach:
$$\text{Required} = \text{Total} - (\text{all nurses}) - (\text{all doctors})$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify complementary cases with no doctors (5C5) or no nurses (7C5).
Subtract bad cases from total selections: 792 - 21 - 1.
Evaluate the difference to obtain 770 committees.

parts.label: c
hints: At least 2 of each profession in a team of 5 leaves only two possibilities.
Either 2 doctors and 3 nurses, or 3 doctors and 2 nurses.
Calculate the number of committees for each case and add them together.
Confirm each product: ${}^7 C_2 \times {}^5 C_3$ and ${}^7 C_3 \times {}^5 C_2$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the two possible distributions:
$$(2\text{D}, 3\text{N}) \quad \text{and} \quad (3\text{D}, 2\text{N})$$

Calculate combinations for both distributions:
$$\text{2D 3N}: {}^7 C_2 \times {}^5 C_3 = 21 \times 10 = 210, \quad \text{3D 2N}: {}^7 C_3 \times {}^5 C_2 = 35 \times 10 = 350$$

Sum the two cases:
$$\text{Total committees} = 210 + 350 = 560$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Break down into the two allowable quotas:
$$\text{Quotas}: \quad (2,3) \; \text{or} \; (3,2)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify valid distributions of doctors and nurses: 2D 3N or 3D 2N.
Formulate sum of products: (7C2 * 5C3) + (7C3 * 5C2).
Sum the cases 210 + 350 to obtain 560 committees.

parts.label: a
hints: Choose 3 red counters from the 7 available red counters.
Choose the other 2 counters from the remaining 9 non-red counters (5 green + 4 yellow).
Multiply the two combinations together.

walkthrough.text:
Select 3 red counters and 2 non-red counters:
$$\text{Red}: {}^7 C_3 = 35, \quad \text{Non-red}: {}^9 C_2 = 36$$

Multiply the selections:
$$\text{Total selections} = 35 \times 36$$

Evaluate the product:
$$\text{Total selections} = 1260$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Structure the selection into red and non-red categories:
$$\text{Selections} = \binom{7}{3} \times \binom{9}{2}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Choose 3 red counters from 7 (7C3) and 2 non-red counters from 9 (9C2).
Formulate the product 7C3 * 9C2 (or 35 * 36).
Evaluate the product to obtain 1260 selections.

parts.label: b
hints: At least 4 of the same colour can occur with red, green, or yellow.
For red: 4 red (and 1 non-red) or 5 red.
For green: 4 green (and 1 non-green) or 5 green.
For yellow: 4 yellow (and 1 non-yellow). 5 yellow is impossible.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate selections with at least 4 red counters:
$$\text{4R 1 non-R}: {}^7 C_4 \times {}^9 C_1 = 315, \quad \text{5R}: {}^7 C_5 = 21 \implies 315 + 21 = 336$$

Calculate selections with at least 4 green counters and 4 yellow counters:
$$\text{Green}: {}^5 C_4 \times {}^{11}C_1 + {}^5 C_5 = 55 + 1 = 56, \quad \text{Yellow}: {}^4 C_4 \times {}^{12}C_1 = 12$$

Sum across all three colours:
$$\text{Total selections} = 336 + 56 + 12 = 404$$

ai_rubric.observable: Partition into cases for at least 4 of each colour: Red >= 4, Green >= 4, Yellow >= 4.
Compute counts: Red (7C4 * 9C1 + 7C5 = 336), Green (5C4 * 11C1 + 5C5 = 56), Yellow (4C4 * 12C1 = 12).
Sum the colour counts 336 + 56 + 12 to obtain 404 selections.

parts.label: c
hints: We require R + G + Y = 5 with each count at least 1.
The partitions of 5 into 3 positive integers are 3+1+1 and 2+2+1.
There are 3 arrangements of 3+1+1 and 3 arrangements of 2+2+1, giving 6 cases in total.
Evaluate ${}^7 C_R \times {}^5 C_G \times {}^4 C_Y$ for all 6 cases and sum.

walkthrough.text:
Sum all 6 cases:
$$\text{Total selections} = 700 + 280 + 140 + 840 + 630 + 420 = 3010$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Enumerate all 6 integer partitions of 5 with each element positive:
$$\text{Partitions}: \quad \{3,1,1\} \text{ and } \{2,2,1\}$$$

Calculate the products for all 6 permutations:
$$700 + 280 + 140 + 840 + 630 + 420$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identify all 6 valid distributions (R, G, Y) with sum 5 and each >= 1: (3,1,1), (1,3,1), (1,1,3), (2,2,1), (2,1,2), (1,2,2).
Evaluate products 7CR * 5CG * 4CY for each distribution: 700, 280, 140, 840, 630, 420.
Sum the counts to obtain 3010 selections.
